description: Digital temperature controllers for 48x48 mm and 48x96 mm panels, Modbus RTU, 2-byte mode
source: Omron, E5@C Digital Temperature Controllers Communications Manual (H175), H175-E1-17

sources.title: E5@C Digital Temperature Controllers Communications Manual (H175)

notes: Uses the manual's 2-byte mode addresses (0x2000 and up), read with function code 03 and written with 06 or 16. The 4-byte mode (addresses from 0x0000, two registers per value) is not mapped; single writes (function 06) work only in 2-byte mode.

Set the protocol to Modbus in the communications setting level first (psel); the factory setting is CompoWay/F. The manual requires 8 data bits for Modbus, with 1 stop bit when parity is even or odd and 2 stop bits when there is no parity. It does not state the factory baud rate or parity in text that could be read; 9600 and even parity are the assumed defaults. The unit number can be 1 to 99 (default 1); 0 is broadcast.

All values are integers with the decimal point left out (105.0 is sent as 1050), negative values in two's complement. For temperature inputs with one decimal, process value, set points and alarm values carry that decimal; the number of decimals follows the input type and is read from Decimal point monitor (0x2410). Their scale is left at 1 for that reason: divide by 10^decimals yourself. MV, heater current and proportional band always have one decimal and use scale 0.1.

Status is a 32-bit word read as two registers: the lower word at 0x2406 (bits 0 to 15) and the upper word at 0x2407 (manual bits 16 to 31, shown here as bit 0 to 15 of that register). Status 2 is at 0x2408 and 0x2409.

Run/stop, auto/manual, AT, multi-SP selection, software reset and similar are operation commands, not registers: write function 06 with address 0x0000 and data = command code in the high byte and related information in the low byte (for example 0x0100 run, 0x0101 stop). Communications writing must be enabled (command 00) before settings can be written. Not modelled as registers. Run/stop and communications-writing state can be read in the status bits.

The manual covers the E5@C family (E5CC, E5EC, E5AC and others) and does not name the E5CC-T and E5EC-T, so they are not listed; some registers apply only to certain models (heater current, remote SP, position-proportional). Written from the manufacturer's document; not tested on a device.
